app.title: Shop Analysis
app.subtitle: Wholesale cosmetics, Algiers
app.error_body: The tool could not finish that. The details below are for whoever set this up.
app.no_data: No data for this period yet.
app.stale_warning: This data is {age} old. The POS may not have saved recently.

today.title: Today
today.subtitle: {date}
today.weekday_avg_note: Average of the last {count} {weekday}s at this time of day
today.compared_at_same_time: All comparisons are cut off at this time of day, so they are fair.
today.quiet_day: Today is running behind a usual {weekday}.
today.good_day: Today is ahead of a usual {weekday}.
today.on_account_note: Money the customer still owes on this period's sales - not counted as a sale until it's actually collected.
today.cash_realized_note: Only Cash, Cheque and Transfer tender counts as a sale here. Anything put on a customer's account is shown separately, on the right.
today.view_tickets: See every ticket in this period

tickets.title: Tickets
tickets.subtitle: Every ticket for the period you choose

trend.title: Trend
trend.subtitle: How the business is moving, month by month
trend.monthly_revenue: Revenue and gross profit by month
trend.incomplete_month: This month is not finished, so it is left out of the comparisons.
trend.heatmap_note: Darker means more sales. Useful for deciding opening hours and staffing.
trend.seasonality_title: Which months are strong and weak
trend.seasonality_note: Average across every year of data. Useful for planning purchases.

cash.title: Cash & P&L
cash.subtitle: What the business earned, and how it was paid
cash.cogs_note: What the goods sold actually cost
cash.working_capital_note: Years of gross profit tied up in stock and receivables
cash.income_statement_title: Revenue, cost and gross profit by month
cash.position_note: All time, split by how the customer paid.
cash.working_capital_explain: Stock plus what customers owe is money already spent that cannot be used elsewhere. Comparing it with a year of gross profit answers: how many years of earnings are tied up in the business right now?
cash.till_note: "Expected" is recomputed from actual tickets, not the POS's own running total. "Recorded" is whatever R.Lynx itself computed when a session closed, not a hand count - so a difference here is not proof of missing cash, only a POS-vs-tickets check. Cash paid out of the drawer (bank drops, float top-ups) is not tracked in this database.

remote.generated_note: This snapshot was generated {when}. If the store PC is off, this page keeps showing this snapshot until it comes back.

customers.title: Customers
customers.subtitle: Who is worth chasing, and who is quietly leaving
customers.pareto_title: How much of the business a few customers make up
customers.pareto_note: Each step along the line is one more customer, biggest first.
customers.pareto_callout: {count} customers make up {share} of your revenue.
customers.call_list_note: Customers who used to buy regularly and have gone quiet. Biggest spenders first. Print this and work down it.
customers.call_list_empty: Nobody has lapsed. Every regular customer has bought recently.
customers.call_list_count: {count} customers to call, worth {revenue} of past business
customers.churn_title: Customers gained and lost each month
customers.walkin_note: The anonymous walk-in till is not counted as a customer. It is {share} of revenue across {tickets} tickets.
customers.detail_never_bought: Has not bought anything measurable yet.

segments.champion_desc: Recent, frequent and big. Protect these.
segments.active_desc: Buying, but not often or not much.
segments.new_desc: Bought for the first time recently.
segments.at_risk_desc: Used to be regular and have slowed down. Call them.
segments.lapsed_desc: Have not bought for a long time. On the call list.
segments.one_time_desc: Bought once and never came back.

receivables.title: Money owed
receivables.subtitle: Cash sitting with customers instead of in your till
receivables.at_risk: Owed by customers who have gone quiet
receivables.concentration_warning: {name} alone holds {share} of everything owed to you ({amount}). If they do not pay, it hurts.
receivables.concentration_ok: No single customer holds a dangerous share of what you are owed.
receivables.months_trade_note: How many months of that customer's own buying the debt is worth. A high number means the debt is large for the size of the customer.
receivables.credit_note: {count} customers are in credit by {amount} in total - they have paid more than they have taken. That is not money you can spend.

inventory.title: Stock
inventory.subtitle: Where your money is sitting
inventory.slow_desc: Last sold between {from_days} and {to_days} days ago
inventory.dead_desc: Nothing sold for {days} days or more
inventory.dead_note: Products sitting on the shelf that nobody has bought for {days} days or more. This is cash you have already spent.
inventory.dead_empty: No dead stock. Everything in stock has sold recently.
inventory.stockout_note: Products that are selling now and have less than {months} months of stock left. Ordered by how much a week without them costs.
inventory.stockout_empty: Nothing is about to run out.
inventory.col_weekly_revenue: A week out of stock costs
inventory.overstock_note: More than {months} months of stock at the current rate of sale. The excess is money you could have used elsewhere.
inventory.negative_note: These products show less than nothing in stock. That is always a recording mistake - goods were sold without being booked in. The stock figure for these cannot be trusted.
inventory.abc_note: A = the products making the top 80% of revenue. C = the long tail.
inventory.shrinkage_note: Totals per physical stocktake, not per product - this database has no line-by-line detail to say which products drove the variance. Different from dead stock: dead stock is unsold but present; shrinkage is stock a physical count found missing (or, when positive, present but not in the books).
inventory.shrinkage_empty: No stocktake has been recorded yet.

catalog.title: Stock catalog
catalog.subtitle: Every product - reference, family, quantity and price.

products.title: Products & margin
products.subtitle: What actually makes money, and what quietly loses it
products.low_margin_note: High revenue but margin below {threshold}. These are where a small price rise is worth the most.
products.low_margin_empty: No high-revenue product is below the healthy margin.
products.below_cost_note: Every one of these lost money on every unit sold.
products.below_cost_empty: Nothing has been sold below cost.
products.drift_title: Cost went up, price did not
products.drift_note: The cost of buying these has risen but you are still selling at the old price. This is how margin disappears without anyone noticing.
products.drift_empty: No product has had its cost rise without a price change.
products.cost_unknown_note: {count} products have no cost recorded, so their margin cannot be worked out. They are left out of every margin percentage.
products.outliers_title: Priced out of line with their own brand
products.outliers_note: Products whose margin trails their own brand/category average by {pp} percentage points or more - not just "below a healthy margin", but an outlier next to their peers.
products.outliers_empty: No product is a meaningful outlier next to its own brand right now.
products.detail_family_compare: This product vs. its brand average
products.detail_family_note: How this one product's margin compares to every other product in {family}.
products.competitor_note: Entered by hand - nothing is scraped automatically. Log what you see when you check a competitor's shelf or price list.
products.competitor_empty: No competitor prices logged for this product yet.
products.competitor_error_invalid_price: Enter a price greater than zero.
products.new_arrivals_note: Ready to paste into a social media post.
products.new_arrivals_empty: Nothing new added to the catalogue in the last {days} days.

suppliers.title: Suppliers
suppliers.subtitle: Who you depend on
suppliers.concentration_note: The share of your buying that goes to your biggest suppliers. High concentration means a problem at one supplier is a problem for you.
suppliers.top_share: Your top {count} suppliers are {share} of your buying.
suppliers.gaps_note: The POS does not record delivery dates, so this is how often you place an order, not how long delivery takes. Only suppliers with two or more dated orders appear.
suppliers.gaps_empty: Not enough dated purchase history to work this out.
suppliers.overdue_note: Marked overdue when it has been more than half again as long as usual since the last order.
suppliers.cost_trend_title: What you spend on stock each month
suppliers.cost_trend_note: Average cost per unit bought. A rising line with flat selling prices means margin is being squeezed.
suppliers.cost_trend_empty: Not enough dated purchase history to show a trend.
suppliers.coverage_warning: Only {share} of purchase lines can be traced to a supplier, and only {date_share} of orders carry a date. The POS does not store a purchase header, so these figures are built from the supplier-item records. Treat supplier totals as a guide, not a full account.
suppliers.transactions_subtitle: Every purchase this tool can group into one transaction, with a drill-down into its lines.

diagnostics.title: What to fix
diagnostics.subtitle: Ranked by money, not by how loud the warning is
diagnostics.working_empty: Nothing stands out as going well yet.
diagnostics.failing_empty: Nothing is failing badly enough to flag. That is a good sign.

margin_below_healthy.title: Your margin is below what this trade needs
margin_below_healthy.statement: Over the last 12 months you sold {revenue} and kept {profit} of it. That is a margin of {margin}, against the {healthy} this kind of wholesale needs to cover costs.
margin_below_healthy.action: Pick the 20 products with the highest revenue and the lowest margin and raise each one by 2 to 3 percent. Customers rarely notice a change that size on a single line.
margin_below_healthy.fix: Getting from {margin} to {healthy} on the same sales is worth {gain} a year.

margin_healthy.title: Your margin is holding up
margin_healthy.statement: Over the last 12 months your margin was {margin}, at or above the {healthy} this trade needs.
margin_healthy.action: Keep doing what you are doing. Watch the products where cost has risen but price has not.
margin_healthy.fix: Holding this margin on next year's sales is worth {gain} of gross profit.

margin_declining.title: Your margin has fallen {months} months in a row
margin_declining.statement: Margin went from {from_margin} in {from_month} to {to_margin} in {to_month}. On your current sales, each point lost is {per_point} a year.
margin_declining.action: Compare your buying prices this month with three months ago on your ten biggest products. If cost went up and your price did not, that is the whole story.
margin_declining.fix: Winning back those {drop} takes {gain} a year straight to your pocket.

revenue_up_profit_flat.title: You are selling more but earning the same
revenue_up_profit_flat.statement: Revenue over the last 3 months is {rev_change} against the 3 months before, but gross profit is {profit_change}. You are doing more work for the same money.
revenue_up_profit_flat.action: This is either discounting or cost creep. Check the discount column on your biggest tickets, then check whether your suppliers raised prices without you raising yours.
revenue_up_profit_flat.fix: If profit had grown with revenue, you would be {gain} better off over those 3 months.

revenue_growing.title: Sales are growing
revenue_growing.statement: Revenue over the last 3 months is {rev_change} against the 3 months before, and gross profit is {profit_change}. Both are moving the right way.
revenue_growing.action: Make sure the products driving this do not run out. Check the stockout list.
revenue_growing.fix: At this rate the next 12 months adds {gain} of gross profit.

receivable_concentration.title: One customer holds most of what you are owed
receivable_concentration.statement: {name} owes you {amount}, which is {share} of the {total} owed to you by everyone. They last bought {last_purchase}.
receivable_concentration.action: Agree a written payment plan with {name} this week. Until it is agreed, sell to them for cash only.
receivable_concentration.fix: Collecting half of what {name} owes puts {gain} back in your hands.

receivables_controlled.title: Money owed is spread sensibly
receivables_controlled.statement: The {total} owed to you is spread across {count} customers, and the biggest single debt is {share} of the total.
receivables_controlled.action: Nothing urgent. Keep watching anyone who goes quiet while still owing.

collection_risk.title: Customers who owe you money and have stopped buying: {count}
collection_risk.statement: Together they owe {amount}. Each has bought nothing for more than {days} days. The longest silent is {worst_name} at {worst_days} days with {worst_amount} outstanding.
collection_risk.action: Telephone every one of them this week, starting with the biggest. A customer who has stopped buying and still owes money is the one most likely never to pay.

customer_low_margin.title: Big customers served at almost no profit: {count}
customer_low_margin.statement: In the last 12 months they bought {revenue} at an average margin of {margin}. The worst is {worst_name}: {worst_revenue} at {worst_margin}.
customer_low_margin.action: Raise your prices to these customers by 3 percent, or stop giving them your keenest prices on the lines where you make nothing. They are big enough to absorb it.
customer_low_margin.fix: Three points of margin on their trade is {gain} a year.

working_capital_tied.title: Too much of your cash is locked up
working_capital_tied.statement: You have {stock} in stock and {receivables} owed to you: {tied} in total. Last year you earned {profit} of gross profit. Your money is turning over {ratio} times slower than it should.
working_capital_tied.action: Attack the two biggest pockets: clear the dead stock and collect the oldest debts. Do not buy more of anything you already have a year of.
working_capital_tied.fix: Freeing a quarter of what is tied up releases {gain} of cash.

working_capital_healthy.title: Your cash is working reasonably hard
working_capital_healthy.statement: You have {tied} tied up in stock and customer debts against {profit} of gross profit last year, a ratio of {ratio}.
working_capital_healthy.action: Keep it there. The main risk is buying stock faster than you sell it.

dead_stock_share.title: {share} of your stock has not sold in {days} days
dead_stock_share.statement: {value} of stock across {items} products has not sold for {days} days or more. That is money you have already paid for, sitting on a shelf.
dead_stock_share.action: Take the 30 biggest dead lines and clear them: bundle them with fast sellers, offer them to the shops next door at cost, or discount them hard. Something is better than nothing.
dead_stock_share.fix: Clearing this at a {discount} discount brings back {gain} in cash.

dead_stock_low.title: Very little of your stock is dead
dead_stock_low.statement: Only {share} of your stock ({value}) has gone {days} days without selling. That is well controlled.
dead_stock_low.action: Keep buying the way you are buying.

stockout_imminent.title: Fast sellers about to run out: {count}
stockout_imminent.statement: Together they bring in {weekly} a week. The most urgent is {top_name}: {top_stock} left, selling {top_rate} a month, worth {top_weekly} a week.
stockout_imminent.action: Order these before anything else. The list is on the Stock screen with a suggested quantity for each.
stockout_imminent.fix: Every week they are out of stock costs {weekly} of sales and {weekly_profit} of profit.

stock_turning.title: Nothing important is about to run out
stock_turning.statement: No fast-selling product is down to less than {months} months of stock.
stock_turning.action: Nothing to do today. Check again after the next big delivery goes out.

silent_margin_erosion.title: Products that cost more than they used to but still sell for the same: {count}
silent_margin_erosion.statement: Your buying price went up on these and your selling price did not follow. The worst is {top_name}: cost went from {top_cost_then} to {top_cost_now} while the price stayed at {top_price}.
silent_margin_erosion.action: Put the price up on these {count} products to restore the margin you had. The list is on the Products screen.
silent_margin_erosion.fix: Restoring the old margin on these is worth {gain} a year at the current rate of sale.
silent_margin_erosion.workings: Sum of (margin lost per unit × units sold per year) = {gain}

selling_below_cost.title: Products sold for less than they cost: {count}
selling_below_cost.statement: These sales lost {loss_abs} between them. The worst is {top_name}, losing {top_loss_unit} on each of {top_units} units. {still_count} are still priced below cost today.
selling_below_cost.action: Fix the price on the ones still below cost today. For the rest, check whether the cost was recorded wrongly or whether somebody is discounting too far.
selling_below_cost.fix: Simply not losing money on these is worth {loss_abs}.
selling_below_cost.workings: Sum of (selling price − cost) × units, where negative = {loss}

family_margin_below_average.title: Products priced below their own brand's average margin: {count}
family_margin_below_average.statement: These look fine on their own, but their brand/category as a whole runs at a healthier margin. The worst is {top_name}: {top_margin} margin against a {top_family} average of {top_family_margin} - a gap of {gap}.
family_margin_below_average.action: Check whether these were priced against an old cost, or simply never reviewed since the rest of the family moved. The list is on the Products screen.
family_margin_below_average.fix: Bringing these up to their family's average margin is worth {gain} a year at the current rate of sale.
family_margin_below_average.workings: Sum of (family margin % − product margin %) × revenue = {gain}

overstock_capital.title: Products with more than a year of stock: {items}
overstock_capital.statement: The excess above a sensible level is worth {value}. This is money you cannot use, sitting in goods you already have too many of.
overstock_capital.action: Stop reordering these until the pile comes down. Push them to your regular customers as a bundle.
overstock_capital.fix: Selling the excess even at cost releases {value} of cash.
overstock_capital.workings: Sum of (stock − 6 months of sales) × cost = {value}

lapsed_revenue_at_risk.title: Regular customers who have stopped coming: {count}
lapsed_revenue_at_risk.statement: These customers bought {revenue} from you in the past and have bought nothing for more than {days} days. While they were active they were worth {monthly} a month between them.
lapsed_revenue_at_risk.action: The call list is ready on the Customers screen with phone numbers, biggest spender first. Ring the top 20 this week. Ask what changed.
lapsed_revenue_at_risk.fix: Winning back a quarter of them is {gain} of sales a year.

top_customer_quiet.title: {name} is one of your biggest customers and has gone quiet
top_customer_quiet.statement: They have spent {revenue} with you and last bought {days} days ago, on {last_date}. They normally buy every {usual} days.
top_customer_quiet.action: Telephone {name} today on {phone}. Something has changed - either a competitor took them or something went wrong with an order.
top_customer_quiet.fix: Keeping them is worth {gain} a year.

revenue_concentration.title: Your top 10 customers are {share} of your revenue
revenue_concentration.statement: {revenue} of your {total} comes from just 10 customers out of {count}. Losing any one of them would be felt immediately.
revenue_concentration.action: Two jobs: look after these 10 personally, and spend some effort finding new accounts so the risk spreads.
revenue_concentration.fix: Losing your single biggest customer would cost {gain} a year.

revenue_spread.title: Your revenue is spread across many customers
revenue_spread.statement: Your top 10 customers are {share} of revenue, out of {count} customers in total. No single loss would sink you.
revenue_spread.action: Nothing to do. This is a healthy position.

customer_churn.title: You are losing customers faster than you are gaining them
customer_churn.statement: Over the last 3 months you lost {lost} and gained {gained} customers. The ones you lost were worth {revenue} in their last 12 months.
customer_churn.action: Ring the lost ones before you spend anything on finding new ones. Winning back a customer who already knows you is far cheaper.
customer_churn.fix: Winning back a third of them is {gain}.

customer_growth.title: You are gaining more customers than you are losing
customer_growth.statement: Over the last 3 months you gained {gained} customers and lost {lost}.
customer_growth.action: Make sure the new ones come back a second time. The second purchase is the one that makes a customer.

seasonality_weak.title: Your weakest months, every year: {months}
seasonality_weak.statement: Across every year of your data, {months} run {gap} below your average month.
seasonality_weak.action: Buy less going into these months, and plan your promotions for them rather than for the months that sell themselves.
seasonality_weak.fix: Not overbuying into a weak month keeps {gain} in cash instead of stock.
seasonality_weak.workings: Average monthly cost of goods × {gap} × the weak months = {gain}

negative_stock.title: Products showing negative stock: {items}
negative_stock.statement: These add up to {units} units and {value} of stock value that does not exist. It means goods went out without being booked in, so your stock figures for these products are wrong.
negative_stock.action: Count these {items} products physically and correct them in the POS. Until then, do not trust any stock figure for them.

champions_strong.title: Customers buying often and in volume: {count}
champions_strong.statement: Your champion group bought {revenue} in the last 12 months, {share} of everything you sold.
champions_strong.action: These are the relationships to protect. Make sure they never find your shelf empty of what they buy.

collections_healthy.title: You are collecting what you are owed
collections_healthy.statement: Customers paid you {collected} off their accounts in the last 12 months against {owed} still outstanding.
collections_healthy.action: Keep the pressure on. The habit is working.

dataquality.title: Data quality
dataquality.subtitle: How much to trust each number on the other screens
dataquality.intro: Your POS records a few things in ways that would give wrong answers if taken at face value. Every one of them is handled by this tool. This page shows what they are and how big they are, so you can see the size of what is being corrected.
dataquality.collections_title: Account payments recorded as if they were goods
dataquality.collections_body: {lines} lines worth {value} are customers paying down what they owe, not sales. Almost all are labelled "Paiement de règlement". If they were counted as revenue they would inflate your sales by {share}.
dataquality.collections_handled: Counted as collections everywhere in this tool. Never included in revenue.
dataquality.collections_other: {count} of these lines have no proper label at all and appear to be notes typed into the ticket: {names}. They carry no value, so they change nothing.
dataquality.header_cost_title: The cost written on the ticket is sometimes zero
dataquality.header_cost_body: {wrong} tickets out of {total} record a cost that does not match their own lines, and {zero} of them record no cost at all. Together they understate your cost of goods by {value}.
dataquality.header_cost_handled: Cost of goods is always added up from the individual lines, never taken from the ticket header. The affected tickets are: {tickets}.
dataquality.returns_body: {lines} lines have a negative quantity, worth {value}. That is {share} of revenue.
dataquality.returns_handled: Kept in the figures, so they correctly reduce revenue and profit, and counted separately here.
dataquality.missing_cost_body: {lines} sale lines worth {value} have no cost against them - mostly the "Article divers" catch-all where a price is typed in by hand. Their profit is unknown, not 100%.
dataquality.missing_cost_handled: Left out of every margin percentage. Their revenue still counts. Your real gross profit could be up to {value} lower than the headline figure.
dataquality.negative_stock_body: {items} products show less than nothing in stock, {units} units in total.
dataquality.negative_stock_handled: Flagged, never quietly set to zero. They are listed on the Stock screen so they can be counted and corrected.
dataquality.stale_last_sold_title: The "last sold" date on products is not always updated
dataquality.stale_last_sold_body: {items} products carry a last-sold date older than sales actually recorded against them, the worst by {worst} days.
dataquality.stale_last_sold_handled: The date of the most recent ticket is used instead. Trusting the product field would have wrongly condemned {value} of live stock across {wrongly} products as dead.
dataquality.purchases_body: This POS does not store a purchase header, so a purchase line by itself does not say who it was bought from or when. Rebuilding the link from the supplier records recovers {share} of lines, and only {date_share} of orders carry a date.
dataquality.purchases_handled: Supplier figures are built from what can be traced and are marked as partial. Nothing is invented to fill the gap.
dataquality.purchases_totals_title: Purchase amounts do not add up
dataquality.purchases_totals_body: The purchase lines total {value}. Everything ever sold cost {expected} including what is still on the shelf, so the purchase total is {ratio} times what it should be.
dataquality.purchases_totals_handled: Purchase amounts are used only to compare suppliers against each other, never as an amount of money spent. Cost of goods and stock value come from the sale lines and the product records, which do reconcile. If you want spend by supplier to be trustworthy, this is the thing to fix in the POS.
dataquality.credit_body: {count} customers have a negative balance totalling {value} - they have paid more than they have taken.
dataquality.credit_handled: Money owed to you counts only positive balances. Credits are shown separately because you cannot spend them.
dataquality.walkin_body: {tickets} tickets worth {value} ({share} of revenue) are recorded against "Client divers", the anonymous walk-in till.
dataquality.walkin_handled: Counted as revenue, but excluded from anything about individual customers, because it is really hundreds of different people.
dataquality.margin_check_body: The profit this tool works out from the lines differs from the profit the POS recorded by {value}, which is {share} of revenue.
dataquality.margin_check_handled: The difference comes entirely from the lines with no cost. The two agree everywhere else, which is a good sign that the reading is correct.
dataquality.tender_title: How well payment amounts add up to the ticket total
dataquality.tender_body: {mismatched} tickets out of {checked} ({share}) have Cash + Cheque + Transfer + On-account that does not match the ticket's own total, by up to {gap}.
dataquality.tender_handled: The cash-realized split always uses the payment total itself as its base, not the ticket total, so this never throws the split off - it only says how often the two disagree.
dataquality.on_account_title: Cross-check: on-account sales against money owed
dataquality.on_account_body: All-time on-account sales of {on_account} minus {collections} collected back leaves an expected {expected} still owed. The Money Owed screen currently shows {actual}.
dataquality.on_account_handled: These are worked out two completely different ways - one from ticket payment amounts, one from customer balances - so they will not match exactly. A gap this size is expected from opening balances and anything adjusted directly in the till software.
dataquality.verification_title: Proof the database is being read correctly
dataquality.verification_note: These figures were checked by hand against your database when the tool was built. The all-time totals should only ever grow, by exactly the value of new sales. If one of them jumps or falls, something is wrong and it should be looked at.

digest.subject: Shop summary for {date}
digest.title: Yesterday at a glance
digest.stockout_alert: {name} runs out in {days} days - worth {weekly} a week
digest.overdue_alert: {name} owes {amount} and has not bought for {days} days
digest.quiet_customer_alert: {name} normally buys every {usual} days and has not been in for {days}
digest.footer: Produced by your shop analysis tool at {time}. Numbers come straight from your POS database.
digest.attachment_note: The full Excel report is attached.

excel.source: From your POS database, last saved {when}
excel.warning_note: Read the Data quality sheet before relying on any single figure.
